description:
## Summary

Nextflow plugin for experimental features that want to become core features. Currently includes automatic deletion of temporary files, JSON/YAML read/write functions, CSV and text file merge operations, HTTP request capabilities, template rendering, and scan operators.

## Get Started

To use `nf-boost`, include it in your Nextflow config and add any desired settings:

```groovy
plugins {
  id 'nf-boost'
}

boost {
  cleanup = true
}
```

## Examples

The plugin includes the following example usage patterns:

**Refactoring splitFastq into a process:**

```groovy
process SPLIT_FASTQ {
  input:
  path(fastq)

  output:
  path(chunks)

  exec:
  chunks = fastq.splitFastq(file: true)
}
```

**Using mergeText to replace collectFile:**

Refer to the `examples` directory for complete example pipelines demonstrating how to use all features in this plugin, including JSON/YAML operations, HTTP requests, template rendering, and the scan operator.

## What's new

**Version requirements:**

| Version | Minimum Nextflow version |
| ------- | ------------------------ |
| 0.8.x   | 25.10 |
| 0.7.x   | 25.10 |
| 0.6.x   | 25.04 |
| 0.5.x   | 24.10 |
| 0.4.x   | 24.04 |
| 0.1.x   | 23.10 |

## Breaking changes

- The `exec` operator was removed in version 0.5.0. Use an `exec` process instead.
- The `then` operator was removed in version 0.8.0.

spec.name: boost
cleanupFailedTasks
spec.description: When `true`, delete the work directory of each failed task attempt that is retried (default: `false`). Requires automatic cleanup to be enabled.

spec.name: cleanup
spec.description:
Set to `true` to enable automatic cleanup (default: `false`). Temporary files will be automatically deleted as soon as they are no longer needed.

Can also be `'v1'` or `'v2'` to use an implementation that works with publishDir or the workflow output definition, respectively. Setting to `true` is equivalent to `'v1'`.

spec.name: cleanupInterval
spec.description: Specify how often to scan for cleanup (default: `'60s'`).
The `boost` scope allows you to configure the `nf-boost` plugin.
